What to do & when
▣ How are the forecast numbers calculated? See the Forecast Logic button on the demand toolbar — it documents the chained last-year rule, new-SKU contribution, overrides, launch/discontinue and smoothing in full.
1 · Data updates — actuals, product & inventory
Automatic. Product data, sales actuals and inventory import into Supabase every day via n8n — no manual extract, upload or rebuild.
Sales lag slightly: actuals still come in manually from Cin7, so the most recent week or two may not be in yet. This tightens up when we move to Fulfil / a more automated feed.
2 · Preorder, Key‑account & everything else
Live in Supabase. Forecasts, POs, shipments, preorders and key-account orders are all read live — no rebuild.
Refresh the page (or BUY tab → Refresh data) to pull the very latest.
3 · Forecasts in PLAN
Each SKU/month is your saved override where you've set one, otherwise the calculated forecast (chained last-year for continuing SKUs, subcategory contribution for new ones — see ▣ Forecast Logic).
Edit any cell to override it (a literal number, or a % growth on last year). Save Forecasts persists your overrides; the buy plan reflects them live.
4 · Buy plan demand
No action needed.
Open BUY — it uses SKU-level forecasts (forecast_outputs) where available, otherwise your live PLAN forecast.
5 · Remove a SKU from the plans
Both plans mirror the product master (the Airtable PIM), imported daily — a SKU shows while it's available for that country/channel and not discontinued.
Hide it now (view only): PLAN — keep the Active only pill on (hides discontinued SKUs). BUY — turn off the DISC status pill.
Remove it for good: in the product master set the SKU's discontinue date (a past date) for that country — or clear its channel availability / remove the SKU. The daily import picks it up automatically (no manual rebuild). Discontinuing drops it from PLAN; clearing availability also drops it from BUY.
6 · How new SKUs get a forecast
A SKU with little or no sales history still needs a number. Two paths, in order:
a) Replacement SKU — if the product master sets a replacement_sku, the new SKU inherits that predecessor's sales history as its forecast basis (applied automatically from the field; the new SKU's own actuals take over month by month as they come in).
b) Subcategory contribution — otherwise the SKU takes a share of its subcategory forecast, scaled by its market tier. Tiers are weighted A / B / C (default 3 / 2 / 1): an A-tier SKU is seeded at 3× the weight of a C-tier one. This is what the BUY plan, the SKU drill-down and the inline expander all use, so a brand-new SKU shows a non-zero number everywhere.
Tier weights:
Only affects SKUs with no history and no replacement. Equal weights (e.g. 1/1/1) gives a flat split; resets to 3/2/1 on reload.
7 · Smoothing (the “smooth” gap button)
When a subcategory's SKU rows don't add up to its forecast, a gap shows on the “↳ N total” line. Click smooth on a month to rescale that month's SKUs so they sum to the subcategory forecast.
It distributes the subcategory target across SKUs in proportion to each SKU's current forecast (a capped proportional fill), with these rules:
  • Pre-launch — a SKU gets 0 for any month before its launch date.
  • Discontinued — past its discontinue date a SKU is capped by remaining stock (on-hand + inbound, run down month by month); it’s never allocated more than it can ship.
  • Black Friday (November) — in November, a discontinued SKU that still has stock is pushed to clear inventory: its weight is set to last November’s actuals + 50% (still capped by remaining stock).
Smoothing writes per-SKU overrides — Save Forecasts persists them. It never exceeds the subcategory total or a discontinued SKU’s stock.
Product, sales actuals & inventory import daily via n8n → Supabase; everything else is live. Your forecast edits save with Save Forecasts (to forecast_outputs). No manual rebuilds.
⚙ Smoothing settings
Saved ✓ — persists per country/channel
Per country / channel / sub-category — every choice is saved to the database and reloads next time. Disregard disc.: smoothing leaves discontinued SKUs at their stock rundown and boosts only active SKUs to sum to the category forecast. Auto: include in the one-click auto-smooth sweep. The sweep first re-caps discontinued SKUs to remaining stock (on-hand + inbound spread across the run-out months, then 0 once exhausted), then rescales only months whose SKU-sum is within the gap threshold (a bigger gap is left for manual review).
Mode — how the rescale is shared out: Standard scales every SKU by the same factor so their sum hits the sub-category target. Leader protects historically-strong SKUs — it floors them at 80% of their historical share (× tier target) so top performers aren’t diluted, and pushes the rest of the adjustment onto the smaller SKUs.

▣ Forecast logic — how every number is calculated
Every SKU × market × channel × month cell is either a real actual or a calculated forecast. The demand plan and the buy plan use the same forecast, so they always agree.
1 · Actuals vs forecast
Months up to and including the last complete month are actuals (read-only). The current (part-way) month and everything after are forecast.
2 · A SKU's forecast — in order of precedence
a) Your override — type in any forecast cell (a literal number, or a % growth on last year). A saved SKU forecast always wins for that month.
b) Continuing SKU (has last-year sales) — chained last-year rule: the same month last year. If that month has fully completed, use its actual (e.g. a Jun-2027 cell uses the Jun-2026 actual). If it's incomplete (e.g. Aug-2026, part-way), use last year's forecast for that month, carried forward. No growth is added by default — growth comes from your overrides or the category assumptions below.
c) New SKU (no last-year sales) — two paths, in order: (i) replacement SKU inherits its predecessor's history (set replacement_sku in the product master); else (ii) subcategory contribution — a share of the subcategory forecast, scaled by market tier A / B / C (default 3 / 2 / 1).
3 · Launch & discontinue
Pre-launch: any month before a SKU's launch date is 0. Discontinued: after the discontinue date the forecast is capped by remaining stock (on-hand + inbound, run down month by month) — never more than it can ship.
4 · Category / subcategory forecast (the cascade)
Set a subcategory's monthly number as a growth % vs last year (e.g. 0.25 = +25%) or an absolute. Where the sum of the SKU forecasts doesn't match the subcategory forecast, a gap shows on the “↳ total” line. Smoothing a month rescales that month's SKUs (in proportion to their current forecast, capped by pre-launch = 0 and discontinued stock) so they sum to the subcategory target.
5 · Committed demand & the buy plan
Committed Preorder & Key-account orders are folded into B2B demand. The buy plan reads these exact SKU forecasts (saved overrides where set, otherwise the chained/cascade rules above), so what you see on the plan is what it buys to.
Tier weights (new-SKU split) are set in the “What to do & when” help (the ? button). Overrides persist with Save Forecasts.
